title: HADES automatic recall score diagnostic
classification: synthetic local diagnostic; not owner dogfood or release qualification

method.diagnostic_fields: Ranks, canonical types, and numeric retrieval scores only; no text, facts, or identifiers.

interpretation: The immediate HADES automatic recall missed the marker and took 28.9 seconds; the paired PLAIN recall found it in 1.8 seconds.
After 43.6 seconds for background work to become idle, HADES found the marker in 10.0 seconds.

The rank-one observation had semantic score 0.629, reranker score 0.019, and final score 0.021. Hindsight v0.10.2 uses the cross-encoder score as its primary relevance signal, then applies multiplicative recency, temporal, and proof-count boosts. The final/reranker ratio here is about 1.1; the large change is between semantic and reranker scores. Because result text was deliberately not retained, this does not prove whether the reranker down-ranked the expected fact.
Ordinary-turn timings are single samples and should not be used to claim a comparative latency win.
limitations: One synthetic paired pass only; no human quality or naturalness ratings.
Staged model weights and runtime do not prove equality with production deployment.
The settled recall followed the HADES idle barrier and is not immediate-turn behavior.
This does not qualify production memory contents, UI authentication, household isolation, or owner preference.
